title: PowerPoint on desktop: reference a PowerPoint file when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The roadmap facts, documented workflow and four control paths and commands check out. However, the briefing says the default is unknown while also promising that licensed desktop users will receive the option without administrator action; that unsupported assurance needs removing.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: A default state specifically for Reference file is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Reference file default; opened release-notes, configure-copilot-admin-center and support.microsoft.com/en-us/powerpoint/edit-with-copilot-in-powerpoint. The latter says Copilot editing is on by default, not specifically Reference file.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an administrator setting specifically for Reference file.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Reference file admin policy default enable disable license pricing fair use; PowerPoint Copilot reference file admin switch Microsoft Graph PowerShell policy. Opened release-notes and configure-copilot-admin-center; no feature-specific setting found.

claims.claim: The release-note entry names no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: licence and license in the complete Reuse content and style entry in microsoft-365/copilot/release-notes. Read its description, What changed, Why, Try this and impact paragraphs; none names a licence.

claims.claim: The release-note workflow adds no new sign-in or consent step.
claims.quote: Searched: sign-in and consent in the complete Reuse content and style entry in microsoft-365/copilot/release-notes. Read both Try this workflows; neither includes a sign-in or consent step.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat (Basic) users do not have access to Copilot in PowerPoint.

claims.claim: The Basic tier's PowerPoint feature list includes creating presentations from prompts or existing content.

claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The overview says some Copilot features are subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly identify the tier for the Reference file capability by that name.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Reference file license; PowerPoint Copilot reference presentation file license tier Basic Premium pricing meter. Opened copilot-overview, the release entry and Create a new presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint; none explicitly assigns Reference file to a tier.

claims.claim: Whether a fair use limit applies specifically to Reference file is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot Reference file admin policy default enable disable license pricing fair use. Opened copilot-overview and support.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-copilot/limits-for-features-copilot-chat; neither identifies Reference file as a limited feature.

claims.claim: No separate meter for this capability is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot reference presentation file license tier Basic Premium pricing meter. Opened copilot-overview and the release entry; usage-based capabilities named in the overview do not include Reference file. No separate meter found.

claims.claim: No separate price for this capability is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot reference presentation file license tier Basic Premium pricing meter. Opened copilot-overview, the release entry and Create a new presentation with Copilot in PowerPoint; no Reference file-specific price found.

claims.claim: The surrounding PowerPoint Copilot licensing has both non-add-on Basic and add-on Premium experiences, described as mixed in the front matter.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps ... Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) is the full add-on licensed experience

claims.claim: Individual licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. ... Select the row of the user ... select Licenses and Apps. ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with UserId, AddLicenses containing SkuId and an empty RemoveLicenses assigns the selected licence.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least a License Administrator or User Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site ... Use PowerShell ... Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: By default only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is an existing site-level control that limits Copilot discovery while permissions are reviewed.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes discoverability, not existing permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery applies to SharePoint sites and is not supported for OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites. It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not affect experiences operating on content already in use by the user.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't affect experiences that operate on content that's already in use by the user, such as summarizing an open document.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not explicitly say whether Restricted Content Discovery blocks a file selected through Reference file.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Reference file Restricted Content Discovery. Opened sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery and the release entry. The restriction concerns tenant-wide discovery and exempts content already in use; neither resolves a file explicitly selected with Reference file.

claims.claim: The Copilot settings page groups settings under User access, Data access, Copilot actions and Other settings.
claims.quote: Browse User access, Data access, Copilot actions, and Other settings. Select View all or All settings when a setting isn't shown in a category.

claims.claim: The cited Copilot settings page lists no setting named for Copilot in PowerPoint or Reference file.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot in PowerPoint, PowerPoint, Reference file and Agent Mode in the complete copilot/implement/configure-copilot-admin-center page. Read all settings tables and Other settings; none names either capability.

claims.where: Why it matters; front matter: defaultState
claims.claim: Despite reporting the arrival default as unknown, the briefing promises that licensed desktop users will gain the option if nobody acts.
claims.quote: defaultState: "unknown"; "Microsoft has not stated whether the capability is on by default or whether an admin setting governs it"; "If nobody acts, licensed users on desktop will gain the option as it rolls out."
claims.fix: Remove 'If nobody acts, licensed users on desktop will gain the option as it rolls out.' Keep the narrower statement that Microsoft has not stated the arrival default specifically for Reference file; the release note supplies user steps, not an automatic-enablement promise.

claims.claim: The checklist directs administrators to fix source-deck permissions, but neither control row documents source-deck permissions.
claims.quote: "fix permissions on the source deck"; the controls table contains only licence assignment and Restricted Content Discovery, which the page itself says changes discoverability rather than permissions.
claims.fix: Remove ', and fix permissions on the source deck' from the After rollout checklist bullet so it asks pilot users to report unexpected exposure without directing an undocumented control change.
